transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

That's almost certainly normal, so you can relax. Most washer dryers, including Beko models, use water during drying.

## Why it uses water

Most washer dryers are water-cooled condenser dryers. Here's how it works:

1. A heater warms air, which is blown through the drum and picks up moisture from the clothes as steam.
2. To get that moisture out of the air, the machine trickles a thin stream of cold water down the inside of the condenser duct or the back of the drum.
3. The hot, damp air hits the cold surface, the steam condenses back into water, and that water (plus the cooling water) is pumped down the drain.
4. The now-drier air is reheated and recirculated.

So the gentle trickling sound and the drain pump running periodically throughout the cycle are exactly what you'd expect. It typically uses somewhere in the region of 10–40 litres over a drying cycle, depending on the model and programme length. That's one reason washer dryers are less efficient than standalone heat pump dryers.

## When it might be a fault

It would be worth investigating if you notice:

• Water visibly pooling in the drum or rising up the door glass
• Clothes coming out wetter than they went in
• Water leaking onto the floor
• The water running constantly at high flow (like a fill for a wash) rather than a trickle
• The cycle never finishing or clothes staying damp after a long time
• An error code on the display

If any of those happen, the cause is often a faulty inlet valve, a blocked drain filter or pump, or a kinked or blocked drain hose.

## Tips for better drying

• Clean the drain filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front) every few months, since lint builds up there in drying mode.
• Don't overload it. Most washer dryers can only dry about half their wash capacity (e.g. a 9kg wash / 6kg dry).
• Use a high spin speed before drying so there's less water to remove.

If you want to double-check, your Beko manual (or the model number on the sticker inside the door) will confirm that it's a water-condensing model.
